largest.sector: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies
largest.title: Power Sector Reform Programme
largest.desc: As part of the FC project, a credit line is being granted to refinance energy projects in the areas of renewable energies (wind and solar), battery storage, transmission and distribution infrastructure and green hydrogen. The project executing agency is the state-owned Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA). For the credit line, the DBSA will be granted a FC development loan of up to EUR 200 million. South Africa is experiencing a severe energy crisis with frequent power cuts (loadshedding), which is slowing down growth and economic recovery and further exacerbating systemic challenges. The JETP Investment Plan from November 2022 is based on the country's National Development Plan (NDP) 2030 and pursues the vision of tackling the country's systemic challenges such as poverty, inequality and unemployment. The JETP investment plan recognizes the energy transition as an opportunity for the country to drive industrial development, innovation and economic diversification to achieve the vision of the NDP. This is where the FC project comes in with the aim of contributing to the expansion and transformation of the energy supply in South Africa in line with the South African Investment Plan for a Just Energy Transition (JET-IP) and the targets for reducing CO2 emissions in accordance with the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). In addition, the project makes a direct contribution to the DC program objective: Germany supports the South African Just Energy Transition to achieve CO2 emission reductions in accordance with the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) by 2030.

largest.sector: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies
largest.title: Renewable Energy and Green Hydrogen Financing Facility (REGHF)
largest.desc: This project aims to contribute to the achievement of the programme objectives of assisting South Africa and the region in achieving its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The project will finance investments in the expansion of electricity generation capacity from renewable energy sources and associated electricity evacuation infrastructure in Cape Town. The city's priority objective is to increase the capacity of the power grid in order to integrate renewable power sources, especially PV and wind power, in the future. However, this requires adapting and expanding the urban network infrastructure. Due to the age of the network infrastructure, high investment in technical equipment is also necessary to maintain the level of electricity availability and related services. This is all the more important in view of the influx of industrial and IT companies and the resulting high-density of electricity demand. The loan will be used to finance many of the city's smaller projects for which selection criteria will apply. If a project falls under one of the following criteria, it can be financed by the KfW loan: high or medium voltage infrastructure, modernisation or maintenance of network infrastructure, or generation of own renewable energy. The project shall also contribute to gender equality as a secondary objective. Cape Town will conduct an analysis that examines the different impacts of public infrastructure on women and men. The aim is to refocus the city's internal processes so that women's needs are taken into account in the planning of future infrastructure projects.

largest.title: Policy-based Loan to support Namibian government budget and economic recovery
largest.desc: The objective of the project is to support the Namibian government in implementing comprehensive structural reforms, particularly in the areas of 'fiscal stability' and 'promoting economic transformation and effective governance'. In particular, the reforms are based on the Harambee Prosperity Plan II (HPP II) adopted by the Namibian government in 2021, in which the Namibian government defined various areas of intervention and backed them up with implementation plans. Upon fulfillment of the policy reforms agreed upon in the Policy Matrix and the implementation steps specified therein, an ODA-eligible development loan will be provided and disbursed to the Republic of Namibia, represented by the Ministry of Finance, as a local currency loan. The 'policy-based financing' approach is intended to support the implementation of reform measures that contribute to the socio-economic development of the country and broad-based economic growth, thereby supporting Namibia in its socio-ecological economic transformation.

rows.title: Policy Reform Loan to support the Just Energy Transition II
rows.desc: The Program supports the GoSA's efforts to advance the restructuring of the power sector to promote long-term energy security and a low carbon transition. The Program builds on recently approved government strategies to respond to the current energy crisis, including the Energy Action Plan as well as key regulatory changes required to transition from a vertically integrated market structure to a more efficient unbundled structure. It was developed in partnership with the World Bank, the AfDB and the Government of Canada under the leadership of National Treasury. Specific initiatives supported by the loan include: the operationalisation of the National Transmission Company of South Africa (NTCSA) as a key enabler to investment in transmission infrastructure that could allow 53 GW of renewable energy generation capacity to be added to the grid by 2032, the Electricity Regulation Amendment Bill which paves the way for a wholesale competitive electricity market which will deepen the participation of the private sector across the electricity value chain, the Eskom Debt Relief Act which seeks to ensure ESKOM and the NTCSA's future financial sustainability, the amendment of Schedule 2 of the Electricity Regulation Act which provides licensing exemption to Embedded Generators to promote electricity generation from private developers, tax incentives for individuals and businesses investing in rooftop solar photovoltaic infrastructure, the Taxation Law Amendment Act which gradually increases the carbon tax rate, increased budgetary allocations and a gradual improvement in its allocation efficiency to cushion poor households against approved above inflationary electricity tariff increases, and the establishment of the Energy Bounce Back Scheme that provides a 20% first-loss guarantee on loans extended by commercial banks to SMEs and individuals investing/leasing renewable energy. The Scheme targets at least 30% participation by women.
